title: Flowise OAuth2 credential refresh -- T1528 an unauthenticated, whitelisted endpoint returns the live access_token in its response body
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70478 (GHSA-qgvm-j2hm-6m38),
affecting Flowise's OAuth2 credential refresh endpoint.

`POST /api/v1/oauth2-credential/refresh/:credentialId` is listed in
`WHITELIST_URLS`, so it requires no authentication at all. It
decrypts the stored credential (`clientId`, `clientSecret`,
`refresh_token`), exchanges the refresh token with the configured
OAuth provider, and returns the new `access_token` DIRECTLY in the
JSON response body. An attacker who obtains any credential ID --
through a public chatflow leak, enumeration, or an unrelated IDOR --
can call this endpoint with no session and no API key, and receive a
live, usable access token for whatever third-party service (Google,
Microsoft, GitHub) the victim credential is connected to.

Detection logic flags a request to this refresh endpoint carrying no
`Authorization` header and no session cookie -- the exact
unauthenticated-reachability this advisory's Docker validation
confirms (`Credential not found`, not `401 Unauthorized`, proving the
endpoint processes the request before any auth check).

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact route file, line numbers, and a Docker-validated
proof distinguishing "credential not found" from "unauthorized"), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
